case_title: V. K. Mishra & Anr. v. State of Uttarakhand & Anr.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304B, s.498A; Dowry Prohibition Act s.3, s.4
aggravating_circumstances: Demand of dowry, cruelty and harassment by husband and in-laws
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 304B, 498A IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, sentenced to life imprisonment and other sentences
neutral_facts: The deceased, Archana, was married to Rahul Mishra in 1997. Prior to and after the marriage, her father gave her dowry, including money and jewelry. Archana complained to her father about harassment and cruelty by her in-laws and husband in connection with dowry demands. She died from poisoning shortly after returning to her parents' house. The father lodged a complaint, and an FIR was registered. The prosecution alleged that the accused subjected the deceased to cruelty and harassment in connection with dowry demands, leading to her death. The accused denied the allegations, but the courts found the prosecution's case credible, based on evidence including witness statements, medical reports, and financial records. The accused were convicted of dowry death and other charges.
